entries.message: <{tag}> has an async connectedCallback, which cannot be awaited during a synchronous render — its markup would be empty.
entries.fix: Use renderToStringAsync, or load data first and pass it as attributes.

entries.message: `attributes` cannot use {name} as a name — an attribute name may not contain whitespace, a quote, "/", "=" or ">"; setAttribute refuses it in the browser too.
entries.fix: Give it a valid attribute name.

entries.message: a "{type}" listener threw — the dispatch went on, as in a browser; its error follows.
entries.fix: The error names what went wrong. This is said once per component and event type for the life of the process.

entries.message: some of this element's markup could not be parsed, so children/querySelector do not see it — they answer emptily, or with only the part that did parse.
entries.fix: This DOM parses markup it can reproduce exactly and declines the rest, rather than building a tree the browser would not — a mismatched or stray closing tag is the usual cause. Make the markup well-formed, or build the children with createElement/appendChild if a component needs to read them back.

entries.message: component nesting exceeded {max} levels. A component that renders itself recurses without bound, and on a server that is a hung request — so this refuses rather than waiting for the stack to go.
entries.fix: If the tree is genuinely this deep it renders fine in a browser, which has no such limit; that difference is in the @verajs/ssr README.

entries.message: no custom element definition found for {url}.
entries.fix: Export the component's class from that module, or pass { tag }.
Check the options passed to renderToString.

entries.message: <{tag}> refused a value from `props` — setting it threw {thrown}.
entries.fix: A read-only property cannot be set; pass it as an attribute, or give the class a setter. The setter's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: <{tag}> threw while rendering{others} — its markup would be empty: {thrown}.
entries.fix: The component's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: the server renderer has been replaced — a renderer was wired that does not know @verajs/ssr is rendering, and every component would render empty.
entries.fix: Import @verajs/ssr BEFORE wiring the renderer: vera's renderer then declines on the server and keeps only its shadow default. A renderer that is not vera's: guard its wiring (`if (!globalThis.__veraSsrShimmed)`).

entries.message: this DOM cannot answer the selector {selector} — {why}.
entries.fix: It matches on structure and attributes only; rather than return a wrong answer it says so.

entries.message: <{tag}> refused the bound property `.{name}` — its setter threw {thrown}.
entries.fix: The binding's value is the argument it was given; the setter's own error is this one's cause.

entries.message: CSSStyleSheet.deleteRule needs a parsed rule list; this sheet is text.
entries.fix: Remove the rule from the text instead, or replace the sheet.

entries.message: this render declared itself static, so its stores are not reactive and writing {prop} would change nothing.
entries.fix: Remove `static: true` from renderToString, or stop writing to the store during the render.

entries.message: hoisted different CSS than it did on an earlier render, and the new stylesheet was dropped.
entries.fix: A tag's styles are established once per class for the life of the process, so CSS that varies per request cannot be hoisted — put the varying part in an inline style or a custom property instead.

entries.message: a template cannot render inside a text-only element (`<textarea>`, `<title>`…) — its content is text.

was served after its {timeout} ms `timeout` with a promise still pending in {pendingIn} (an async connectedCallback, or a promise a frame callback returned), so the page is what had rendered by then. Still waiting on customElements.whenDefined for {waitingOn}, which the server never defined.
entries.fix: If only the browser defines it, return before that wait on the server — `if (globalThis.__veraSsrShimmed) return;` — so the server serves what the component shows before the wait, as the browser does first. Raise `timeout` if the wait is real, or find the promise that never settles. Said once per component for the life of the process.

entries.message: a template cannot end inside a tag — the client drops an unfinished tag.
entries.fix: Close the tag inside the template.
Nothing was imported. A module URL is bounded to `base`; point it at a module inside that directory.
